acts.name: Price: costs, the real problem, mastery
Proof under pressure: crisis, climax, aftermath

loops.what: Eyes/brain/reflexes stay normal ('remember that') -> tunnel vision and 14 m reaction distance become the real problem
Ball left behind at soccer -> the kid's ball is the one thing not saved in the rescue
300 m braking distance -> you start braking exactly 300 m out in the climax
Track spikes bought for grip -> spikes dig in, sparks, melted flat
Rule 'slow down before you need to' -> the rescue is literally a slow arrival
Mom's giant cereal -> mom with a cereal spoon gives the blessing
Villain the mind-reader can't read + stopped highway -> Stop Time episode

beats.summary: Late for school with one minute left; you leave home and are seated before the bell. A classmate can't process it.
The title question spoken word for word, followed by the 'here is how it works' pivot.
visual: title card over aerial suburb establishing shot

beats.summary: Exactly what changes: the legs, every stride ten times quicker; nothing else looks different.
The limit is planted early: senses and reaction speed stay human, and the narrator flags it as important for later.
visual: navy card: stick figure with brain, eye and reflex icons

beats.summary: Normal teen sprint to new top speed, then three comparisons that climb: highway car, race car, the world's fastest sprinter, and a 100 m time vs the world record.
Track trials: the coach blows the whistle, looks at the stopwatch, looks up, and you are already holding his water bottle. He demands a rerun you already did.
Real research: what limits sprinters is how fast muscles fire, measured as foot-ground contact time; yours is ten times shorter, so your steps sound like a drum roll.
visual: navy card: stride diagram with timer

beats.summary: Chore speed-run before the ad break ends, then a pizza-delivery job where you beat the kitchen; customers react.
First soccer game: you outrun everyone to the goal and leave the ball at midfield. Small, funny preview of the power's limits.
Weekend lunch in a city 100 km away and back before a delivery would arrive. Scale jumps from town to region.
'But then' the problems start; the first one is the air.
visual: navy card: running figure with wind lines 250 KM/H

beats.summary: Problem 1, air: hurricane-strength wind; drag grows with the square of speed, so ten times faster means a hundred times the push. Four quick body gags.
Cheap workaround: swim goggles, arms tucked, leaning like a bullet; it looks silly and it works. Aside that answers the obvious viewer question (no sonic boom; you would need 50x).
Problem 2, shoes: soles gone within a week; mom counts the pairs.
Problem 3, food: a worked calorie sum (weight x distance) gives seven normal days of food per day; triple breakfast; mom buys cereal boxes the size of an appliance.

Turn inside the turn: none of those costs matter, stopping does. Callback to the planted limit: tunnel vision plus a fifth-of-a-second reaction means 14 m travelled blind. A dog near-miss you survive by luck.
Braking takes 300 m; a full-speed turn needs a kilometre-wide curve. Try-fail: you miss your own street and end up in a neighbour's inflatable pool.
visual: navy card map grid with corners

beats.summary: Learn from nature: the cheetah grips like cleats and steers with its tail. You buy spikes, practise leaning, and friends build a red danger-corner map. Theme rule stated: slow down long before you need to.
'For a while it works' bridge, then a Saturday: a kid chases a ball into the road while a distracted truck driver rounds the corner.
The maths of the problem: you can be there in seconds, but arriving at full speed means you either overshoot or become the impact that hurts him.
You execute the learned rule: straight line, start braking at exactly the planted distance, sparks and smoke, arrive at walking pace. Kid safe, ball flattened.
Cost on the body (melted spikes, shaking legs), a crying grateful mother, and a viral clip whose name turns the theme into an ironic headline.
Night knock; you open before the second knock. A stranger in a gray coat has watched your clip many times and has been keeping tabs on 'all of you'.

Team reveal at the van: telekinetic kid, flyer, mind-reader, home-made beetle armour guy, super-strong red cap. Each gets one quick gag. The organisation is named and the pitch is a three-part list ending in what you add.
You look at the van, your melted spikes, and mom with a cereal spoon, who gives a one-line blessing.
Every phone alarms; the mind-reader is scared because the new threat has no readable thoughts. Live feed: highway cars stopped in mid-air and one figure staring into the camera.
Two questions (what would you do first; who is the villain), subscribe, series tagline.
